newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, Sept breaks resistance.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, Sept breaks resistance.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Friday in a sluggish session, with a late wave of short covering and fund buying driving September through key technical resistance, industry sources said.
September rallied 6.2 cents to close at $2.239 per million British thermal units. October settled 6.9 cents higher at $2.245. Others ended mixed, with some 1999s losing ground.

"We hit some late (buy) stops above $2.21 (basis September) and panicked the shorts, and I think commodity funds are starting to buy," said one Midwest trader, noting September clearly settled above the down trendline from May.
But he said further upside was still in question.

"If the (hot) weather returns, we could get more movement higher, but right now, there's no weather and there was no volume on this move," he said, adding a higher close Monday would help the bullish cause.

Despite a brief weekend warmup in the Midwest and East, forecasters are calling for mostly seasonal to below-seasonal weather early next week. But end-week forecasts vary, with at least one meteorologist expecting another bout of heat in the East, traders said.

Technical traders said September's close today above $2.20 was bullish and should lead to a test of next resistance at the $2.27 double top. Further selling should emerge in the $2.325-2.33 area. Near-support was pegged at $2.15-2.16 and then along the short-term up trendline in the $2.11 area. More important support was expected at $2.08 and then at last week's low of $2.045.

In the cash Friday, Gulf Coast weekend gas was steady to up slightly at about $2.20. Midcon pipes showed similar movement to the mid-teens. New York city gate weekend prices also were modestly higher in the mid-$2.40s.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip jumped 3.7 cents to $2.259. NYMEX said 19,161 contracts traded, about half Thursday's revised tally of 38,622.

On the KCBT, September finished 5.1 cents higher at $2.116, while deferreds ended up by one to 4.4 cents. The East/West spread widened by 1.1 cents to 12.3 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 238 contracts traded, down slightly from Thursday's total of 261.
